text:
a lot of ideas/pitches that appear fundamentally driven, or at least ones I've seen recently, are all fighting against some structural, secular, or industry-level headwind

stuff like: 
-anything AI/LLM impacted (software, consulting, fintech)
-anything GLP1 impacted

there's prob more "current themes" but anything like these, an entire 5-10 pitch can be reduced to 1-2 questions or sentences

ie..."your pitch is that company X is immune to headwind Y, and that the market is wrong to have taken the multiple from [20x] to [10x]."

the important thing is to recognize that this is some huge % of the bet you're making, say 50-95%, so you aren't spinning your wheels on shit that isn't directly linked to "what matters"

pages and pages of "here's why X has been a good business historically" are mostly irrelevant, u aren't addressing what the market seems to believe has changed.

I don't have an answer as to how these resolve, I wrote 3 articles just poking around, the common theme being that these are situations driven by a terminal value overhang

but a pitch that doesn't understand which year(s) of the DCF are impacted, is a pitch that is basically DOA...
